title: Tile objects: one rebuild per remesh, in-place MultiMesh updates, light-only refresh
player_outcome: Trees, furniture and torches no longer flicker or hitch when nearby terrain remeshes (mining, torches, water). Objects update smoothly.
design: Checked in code: TileObjectRenderer marks a chunk dirty on both MeshReady and BodyBuilt (TileObjectRenderer.cs:46-47), so it rebuilds twice. Each rebuild QueueFrees and recreates every MultiMeshInstance3D and MultiMesh with per-instance interop calls, allocates new List and Dictionary objects, and is budgeted by count (8 chunks per frame).

Split the file: TileObjectRenderer.cs keeps events and scheduling; new TileObjectRenderer.Groups.cs does group build and update. Per chunk keep Dictionary<(TileObjectDef, int Variant), Group>. A Group holds its MultiMeshInstance3D, MultiMesh, a reusable float[] buffer, capacity, and its Flames node.

Dirty kinds per chunk: Structure (Added / Removed / Interaction.StateChanged → regroup), Placement (BodyBuilt → recompute transforms), Light (MeshReady with unchanged geometry → custom data only). On MeshReady for a chunk where Colliders.IsPending(coord) is true, wait for BodyBuilt so the chunk rebuilds once.

Update in place: reuse group nodes. Grow MultiMesh capacity by 1.5× and use VisibleInstanceCount. Write transforms and light custom data into one float[] and call RenderingServer.MultimeshSetBuffer once. Remove groups that disappeared. Rebuild Flames only when flame bases change.

Budget by time from runtime.Budgets.ObjectsMs (at least one chunk per frame), chunks nearest the camera first, reusable collections. Timer gd.objects.rebuild; probes objects.rebuilds and objects.light_refreshes.
files_modify: game/World/TileObjectRenderer.cs — dirty kinds, coalescing with colliders, time budget, reusable collections
game/World/WorldRuntime.cs — expose per-chunk mesh change info (geometry changed or collider pending) to subscribers
files_add: game/World/TileObjectRenderer.Groups.cs — in-place group build and update, buffer writes, flames
tests: Smoke builder.cmds, town.cmds, basic.cmds keep their objects.count and objects.instances asserts
perf.cmds: after 10 torches, `assert objects.rebuilds <= 14` and `assert objects.light_refreshes > 0`; `assert perf.max.gd.objects < 6`
verification: Headless smoke passes; rendering run: no gd.objects entries in perf spikes while walking through forest or placing torches
Visual: doors toggle, wired torches turn off, trees sit on smoothed ground (P1b-04), and chests and furniture light up next to new torches
risks: Placement transforms depend on colliders: the coalescing must still rebuild after BodyBuilt
Instance-count growth must not leave stale instances visible (set VisibleInstanceCount)
P1b-13 also edits this file to handle pending models: sequence
